development: Consumed V2 evidence exposed a 17-digit exercise regression offset by 12 gains. Development replays extended compact regions to a major sixth, explicitly preserved generated classic idiom digits after a per-piece repertoire failure, and counted repeated attacks after adding consumed Czerny revealed a two-digit aggregate loss. Attempts are retained. No fresh Schumann scores have been observed. The final consumed replay passes every nonfresh gate against the released baseline.
idioms: Unchanged input-only recognition except compact regions permit at most five distinct pitches within nine semitones and five white-key coordinates. Local recognition requires at least four attacks, including repetitions/oscillations; four distinct pitches are unnecessary for a stable hand position. Chromatic recognition is unchanged. No song, source or family names or reference labels enter the algorithm.
constraints: A complete classic hand supplies generated digit constraints for recognized protected contacts, including all tie/unison aliases. Genuine source anchors retain priority and provenance; caller input is unchanged. The one exact physical search optimizes the remaining general contacts with unchanged Parncutt coefficients and scoring. Explicit whole-hand fallback remains on search failure. Protected costs alone did not preserve protected digits across neighboring contexts.
scope: The native sequence objective is eligible only in fully monophonic physical phrases. Real hand silence separates phrases; a phrase with simultaneous or overlapping contacts retains classic generated digits. A chord in a separate phrase cannot disable an earlier eligible line. Source-only development inspection found whole-hand gating too broad; the regional rule passes every consumed gate before fresh inference. No song/family lookup.
evaluation: Compare released origin/main (8ec11658) and frozen V3 on all consumed Hanon, Beringer, Czerny and Burgmuller cases and both new reservations. Verify the branch classic baseline produces identical planned notes to the released module on every supported case. Record revision and module hash. Keep unsupported pieces in all denominators. Reserved repertoire uses the same fixed 120 BPM profile for both methods. All physical and identity checks remain required. No training or coefficient fitting.
gates: Require strict aggregate printed-digit improvement across both fresh collections and nonregression separately in Schumann and Op840; nonregression in every consumed family and printed/fresh whole-case, whole-hand, adjacent-transition and coverage totals. Additionally require per-case digit, complete-case, complete-hand, transition and coverage nonregression for every consumed scale, chromatic, five-finger and repertoire case. Zero physical conflicts required. Report piece-level changes and uncertainty; do not claim universal musical superiority from reference agreement.
activation: Do not ship published weights or change the product default as part of this research iteration. Report benchmark outcome distinctly from production activation. The existing upstream code/model terms boundary remains unchanged. No human review prerequisite is added.
